title: GB Grid Code, European Connection Conditions (ECC), Issue 6 Revision 33 (11 June 2025): fast fault current injection, faults over 140 ms, excitation and PPM voltage-control performance
source: the ECC section of the GB Grid Code as published by NESO (Issue 6 Revision 33, 11 June 2025), the same issue as gb-ecc-issue6-rev33
pages: page is null for every value: NESO publishes this section as a Word document, whose page numbers depend on how it is rendered, so each value is located by its clause and figure
notInIssue: the GC0111 consultation drafts carried an 'observable within 30 ms' rule and a rule on the average over 30 to 60 ms; neither is in Issue 6 Revision 33, so neither is checked

ffci.gridFormingText: a unit operating in a Grid Forming Capability mode is under ECC.6.3.19 instead (ECC.6.3.19.5, GBGF fast fault current injection, not transcribed)
ffci.unbalancedText: for an unbalanced fault the reactive current must rise with the fall in the retained unbalanced voltage up to its maximum; no envelope is given, so this check covers balanced faults only

retainedVoltageLine.text: the two labelled points of the heavy black line (the figure is marked NOT TO SCALE; the line between them is straight as drawn): reactive current IR in pu of the rating against the retained voltage at the connection point. Interpretation: for a pre-fault reactive current above -0.312 pu the line is taken from (0.9 pu, the pre-fault current) to (0.5 pu, 1.0 pu), GridSim's reading of ECC.6.3.16.1.3 (IR shall as a minimum increase with the fall in the retained voltage, and depends on the pre-fault operating condition)

envelope.text: the edge of the forbidden operating area as a fraction of the increase dIR = IR - IR(pre-fault), from fault inception (the voltage first below 0.9 pu): the labelled points 20, 60, 120 and 140 ms and 0.65 dIR, joined by straight lines as drawn (NOT TO SCALE)

blocking.text: after fault clearance blocking is permitted (the hatched area), so no envelope applies after clearance

ffci.agreedDeviationsText: transient or marginal deviations below the shaded area may be agreed with the company; this check does not allow for any

frtLong.hvdcText: for HVDC equipment the requirement for dips over 140 ms is set in the Bilateral Agreement; no value is shipped

profiles.appliesTo: Type C and D synchronous power generating module
profiles.text: a voltage-duration profile: each point is a dip level and how long it must be ridden through. The labelled corners are transcribed; the figure is marked NOT TO SCALE, so a duration strictly inside a sloped segment has no labelled voltage

profiles.appliesTo: Type C and D power park module
profiles.text: a voltage-duration profile: each point is a dip level and how long it must be ridden through. The labelled corners are transcribed; a duration strictly inside a sloped segment has no labelled voltage

avr.text: open circuit, a step from 90 % to 100 % of nominal terminal voltage: a damped oscillatory response; the terminal voltage first reaches 100 % in less than 0.6 s and settles within 5 % of the voltage change in less than 3 s

vctrl.text: an on-load step in connection-point voltage: the reactive response commences within 0.2 s (i); 90 % of the change in 1 s for a step from zero to the maximum, 2 s from maximum leading to maximum lagging (ii); within 5 s of reaching 90 %, the peak to peak magnitude of any oscillations less than 5 % of 'the change in steady state maximum Reactive Power' (iv), read here as the steady-state change of the step
vctrl.mvarSecondsText: the MVAr-seconds rule compares with a ramp from 0.2 s to 'the required response at 1 second', whose level the figure does not label; not evaluated
